He demanded an impartial investigation, warning that Hindus would not tolerate corruption in the name of religion. The controversy has led to arrests and prompted resignations, with wider scrutiny now on temple donation management.

The movement comes amid heightened Russia-NATO tensions, with reports suggesting NATO navies shadowed the vessel during its journey through the Baltic before it reached northern Russia.

articles.title: Israel scrambles wildly after 'NYT' drops major Iran bombshell
articles.description: A fresh war of words has erupted after Israel rejected a New York Times report claiming Iranian nuclear negotiators were targeted in alleged assassination plots. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office dismissed the report as "fake news," while the newspaper said it stands by its reporting based on multiple current and former U.S. officials. Meanwhile, Iran's Intelligence Ministry has vowed revenge for the killing of Ali Khamenei, blaming both Israel and the United States. Could this escalating rhetoric trigger another dangerous chapter in Middle East tensions?

articles.title: 'He Knows Who The Boss Is': Trump Reminds Bibi
articles.description: Donald Trump says he could meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House after the NATO summit, declaring that Netanyahu "knows who the boss is." Trump also commented on Iran, ongoing diplomatic efforts, and the funeral of Iran's late Supreme Leader, adding fresh intrigue ahead of a potentially pivotal U.S.-Israel meeting.

articles.title: Why Turkey's new war-ready Tayfun Blok-3 could spell trouble for Israel
articles.description: Turkey has declared its indigenous Tayfun Blok-3 ballistic missile ready for operational deployment after a successful live-fire test over the Black Sea. The advanced missile, developed by Roketsan, is designed to strike moving maritime targets with high precision, reinforcing Ankara's growing defence capabilities amid heightened regional tensions and sharp rhetoric between Turkey and Israel.

articles.description: US President Donald Trump marked America's 250th independence anniversary with a patriotic speech on the National Mall, celebrating the nation's enduring spirit and strength. Despite severe storms briefly disrupting the event and forcing an evacuation, thousands gathered for the occasion. Trump lauded veterans and the country's founding principles, while also weaving in partisan themes ahead of upcoming elections. Celebrations across the US were impacted by extreme weather.

articles.title: President Trump extols America, rails at communism in USA 250 celebrations
articles.description: Speaking at Mount Rushmore, President Trump warned against a resurgent "communist menace," including from "newcomers" embracing opposing ideologies. He urged Americans to protect founding freedoms, linking progressive Democratic victories to this threat. Trump vowed to "vanquish communism quickly" and send those embracing it "away," asserting America will never be communist, as he rallied supporters ahead of midterm elections.

articles.title: India slips to 125th in Global Passport Index 2026, offers visa-free access to 26 destinations
articles.description: India's passport has dropped to 125th globally in the 2026 rankings, offering visa-free access to only 26 destinations. This marks a decline from last year's position, placing it behind several nations including the Philippines and Morocco. While India outranks some South Asian neighbours like Nepal and Bangladesh, it still requires visas for major global powers. European nations continue to dominate the top spots in global travel mobility.

articles.title: ‘We Want Fireworks!’: Laura Loomer’s Savage Nudge At Netanyahu To ‘Quickly Bomb’ Khamenei’s Funeral
articles.description: Far-right activist and longtime Donald Trump ally Laura Loomer has ignited a major controversy after a series of social media posts about the funeral of former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Loomer referred to the funeral as a "target rich environment," suggested the Israel Defense Forces had "the opportunity to do the funniest thing," and later wrote that she would "never say no" to seeing the U.S. or Israel bomb "a bunch of jihadis."Her latest remarks came after another viral post in which she reacted to footage of mourners chanting "Death to America" by asking, "Speaking of fireworks... where is the IDF when you need them?" The comments have fueled intense debate online, with supporters defending her stance and critics accusing her of encouraging violence amid already heightened tensions between Israel and Iran.
